business_problem: CG wanted to get users connected as quickly as possible and chose Amazon Rekognition. Chamberlain Group (CG) wanted to expand the number of devices connected to its myQ app for monitoring and controlling garage doors.
solution_summary: Chamberlain Group (CG) wanted to expand the number of devices connected to its myQ app for monitoring and controlling garage doors. To meet this challenge, CG turned to Amazon Web Services (AWS) and added Amazon Rekognition —used to automate and lower the cost of image recognition and video analysis with machine learning—as middleware into myQ. Previously, customers had to search a list to see if their device could connect to the myQ app and then find and follow instructions to connect. CG wanted to get users connected as quickly as possible and chose Amazon Rekognition. “We already used AWS for our video and camera infrastructure,” says Benjamin Hunt, video, artificial intelligence, and middleware developer at CG.

solution_components.name: Amazon Rekognition
solution_components.role: Analyzes images and video to classify or identify physical devices.

business_outcome: Amazon Rekognition uses video images to determine whether the device can connect. “Anyone with a garage door opener, regardless of the brand, can scan it and connect it to our system,” says Jishnu Kinwar, vice president of advanced products at CG.
metrics: CG, a global leader in intelligent access, was founded in 1954 and has products in more than 50 million homes across the United States.
Its myQ app has over 11 million users and counting, plus 8.4 million connected garage door openers.
After initial testing, CG’s myQ solution using Amazon Rekognition was in production within 1 month, and the new features went live in November 2023.
